en.headline: Salmonella found in Wan Chai Hainan chicken rice sample
en.dek: The Centre for Food Safety said a ready-to-eat sample from a restaurant in Tin Lok Lane failed microbiological guidelines and the dish was taken off sale.
body: The Centre for Food Safety said on Wednesday that a Hainan chicken rice sample taken from a restaurant in Tin Lok Lane, Wan Chai, was found to contain Salmonella.

The centre said the pathogen was detected in a 25-gram portion of the ready-to-eat food, exceeding the Microbiological Guidelines for Food, which require Salmonella not to be found in such samples. Officers visited the premises, told the operator of the breach, and the restaurant stopped selling and discarded the affected food as instructed.

Staff were given food safety and hygiene advice. The centre required the restaurant to improve its cooking process and carry out thorough cleaning and disinfection. Local reports named the premises as Keung Kee Restaurant.

The centre said Salmonella infection can cause fever and gastrointestinal illness, including vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhoea, and may be more severe for infants, older people and people with weaker immune systems. It said it would continue to follow up. Under the Public Health and Municipal Services Ordinance, food sold in Hong Kong must be fit for human consumption.

zh.headline: 灣仔海南雞飯樣本驗出沙門氏菌
zh.dek: 食安中心指天樂里食肆即食樣本不符合微生物指引，食肆已按指示停售及棄置相關食品。
body: 食物安全中心星期三表示，在灣仔天樂里一間食肆抽取的海南雞飯樣本驗出沙門氏菌。
中心指，25克即食食物樣本含沙門氏菌，超過《食品微生物含量指引》不得檢出該菌的準則。人員已到場調查並告知違規事項，食肆已按指示停售及棄置相關食品。
中心向食肆負責人和員工作出食物安全及衞生教育，並要求改善烹調流程及徹底清潔消毒。本地報道指涉事食肆為強記飯店。
中心表示，感染沙門氏菌可引致發燒及腸胃不適，包括嘔吐、肚痛及腹瀉，對嬰幼兒、長者及免疫力較弱人士影響可能較嚴重。中心會繼續跟進。根據《公眾衞生及市政條例》，在香港出售的食物必須適宜供人食用。
